High Court Hears Constitutional Challenge to Australia's Under-16 Social Media Ban

03 Nov 2026, 03:18 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.abc.net.au

2 min read

Key takeawaysAustralia's under-16 social media ban is facing its first major legal challenge in the High Court. Advocacy group the Digital Freedom Project and online platform Reddit have brought separate legal bids, which have been joined into a single special case, arguing that the legislation is unconstitutional.

Australia's under-16 social media ban is facing its first major legal challenge in the High Court. Advocacy group the Digital Freedom Project and online platform Reddit have brought separate legal bids, which have been joined into a single special case, arguing that the legislation is unconstitutional.

Overview of the Policy and Legal Arguments

The policy, which took effect in December, requires designated platforms to take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under the age of 16 from holding accounts. Nearly 5 million accounts have reportedly been blocked across ten affected platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Snapchat, X, TikTok, YouTube, Kick, Reddit, and Twitch.

The core legal argument presented by the plaintiffs is that the ban places an unreasonable burden on the implied freedom of political communication under the Australian Constitution by excluding young people from civic engagement.

  • Digital Freedom Project: Argues there is a fundamental disconnect between the law's intent and reality, noting that minors bypass age-assurance checks and that alternatives exist with a lesser burden on communication.
  • Reddit: Contends that the law deprives young people of speaking and organizing avenues, and separately seeks a declaration that it is not covered as an "age-restricted social media platform." Reddit has stated it will continue to comply with the ban while the legal challenge proceeds.

Government Position and Expert Context

The Commonwealth defends the legislation, arguing that the burden on political communication is modest, indirect, and justified to protect children from online harms associated with engagement-driven platform features. The government maintains that constitutional political communication freedoms apply specifically to eligible voters.

Legal experts note the case will clarify the extent of government regulatory power over online spaces. International organizations, including the Free Speech Union, NetChoice, and the Electronic Frontier Foundation, have sought to participate as friends of the court, while state and territory attorneys-General support the Commonwealth.

Verification and Practical Implications

Hearings are scheduled to continue in the High Court. Official updates, court transcripts, and filings can be verified through the High Court of Australia website and official government announcements regarding digital safety policies.
